subject: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmebank.com>
Cc: CloudMate Ops <partner-ops@cloudmate.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments

Team / Sam —

We need to lock down the maintenance plan for Acme Bank's private VPC upgrade next month. The main ask from Acme is that we provide a low-risk version-shelving strategy (ephemeral pinning) that allows us to rapidly unpin and restore the prior runtime in under 10 minutes if any customer-affecting regression appears.

Attached is a first draft of the "ephemeral pin contingency ladder" (ephemeral_pin_contingency_ladder.pdf) and a short rapid-unpin checklist (rapid_unpin_checklist.md). Key points for review:
- Canary window: 30m canaries on a 5% traffic shard, followed by 2 rolling waves (50% then 100%) if metrics pass.
- KV cache compatibility: any unpin must ensure KV cache integrity; plan suggests draining new KV writes to a fallback path during canary.
- Network cutover: two-stage LB shift (internal then external) to keep sessions attached to surviving replicas during rollback.
- Rollback time SLO: recover to previous pinned version within 10 minutes from decision to unpin; scripts in rollback-scripts.tar.gz.

Please review and call out any missing gating metrics we should require from Acme's side (SRE/Oncall), particularly around session affinity and cross-AZ drain time. Sam — can you confirm if the requested 10-minute rollback SLO is acceptable to you and whether Acme needs an earlier freeze on schema or runtime changes?

Next steps: aim to finalize plan by EOD Wednesday so we can ship the runbook to Acme and schedule the maintenance window for Aug 14 (US morning).

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: ephemeral_pin_contingency_ladder.pdf, rapid_unpin_checklist.md, rollback-scripts.tar.gz

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmebank.com>, CloudMate Ops <partner-ops@cloudmate.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments

Neha — quick thoughts after skim:

1) KV cache: we should avoid dual-writes in canary; better to route mutable writes to a write-through proxy that mirrors to both versions for 30m, then cutover reads. That reduces dual-writes risk.
2) Health gates: add application-level correctness checks (end-to-end inference sanity) in addition to 5xx rates and latency p95. If we see model hallucination regressions the rollback should be immediate.
3) Network: for cross-AZ rollback, the LB drift window is the risk. We should include an emergency NLB failback to previous ASG that has auto-warmed instances.

I'll sketch an updated timeline and a minimal operator playbook with command snippets for the 10-minute unpin path.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmebank.com>

Cc: CloudMate Ops <partner-ops@cloudmate.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments

Thanks Neha — Acme SRE here. The 10-minute rollback target is tight but acceptable if Rx is:
- You run the canary in our staging fleet for 48h prior to the window (we already have a staging mirror).
- You provide a validated automation path (scripted) to unpin and shift LB that we can exercise in table-top drills.
- We need a documented freeze: no schema or model runtime changes 72h before the window.

A few clarifications:
- Session affinity: our sessions are sticky for 15 minutes by cookie; we can accept a brief failure as long as SLOs return within 5m after rollback.
- KV durability: we cannot accept any KV loss; reads can be stale for up to 60s, but writes must be replicated synchronously to the fallback path.

We can support Aug 14 morning US if you lock the plan by Wednesday EOD.

Sam
Sam Ortiz
Principal SRE, Acme Bank
sam.ortiz@acmebank.com

Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments

High-level confirmation and a few operational specifics:

- Canary cadence: change to 3 x 10m micro-canaries across different availability zones (reduces blast radius and shortens detection time).
- Automation: I've added a fast-path CLI (redwood-ops rollback-unpin --now) to the runbook; it runs the unpin, flips the LB, and triggers sanity checks. See step 2.1 in the attached runbook.
- Telemetry: add a synthetic inference check (predefined prompt set) that runs every 60s during the window; any fail => immediate abort and rollback.

I've updated the attached PDF and included a minimal operator checklist. Rishi — can you validate that the rollback CLI won't leave zombie state in the orchestration layer? If not, call for a short drain + node-replace step in the checklist.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

> On Mon, Jul 21, 2025 at 11:18 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ephemeral pinning & rapid-unpin contingency ladder for Private deployments

Checked the rollback CLI and runbook. Notes:

- The CLI uses a transactional state file (shelve-state.json) stored in the customer's KMS-backed S3 namespace; the atomic write guarantees we can resume rollback steps if a control-plane node fails.
- I added a final verification step that replays the last 60s of inference traffic on a warmed replica to validate behavior post-unpin. That is necessary to meet Acme's requirement of SLO return within 5m.
- Edge case: if the LB flip fails, we have a fallback toggle via CloudMate's cross-connect (partner-ops) that performs an immediate route reflect to the old ASG. Included contact card for on-call.

Sam — assuming the 72h freeze on schema/runtime changes is OK, we can lock the plan. If you approve, I'll schedule a dry run in your staging fleet on Aug 7 and the live window on Aug 14 (US morning).

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Engineer, Private Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
